title: INNER JOIN: Matching Rows Across Tables 🤝
description: Combine rows from two tables when they share a common key using INNER JOIN.

slides.title: INNER JOIN Syntax 📝
slides.content:
# The Most Common Join

`INNER JOIN` (or simply `JOIN`) returns only rows where the condition is true in both tables.

```sql
SELECT column_list
FROM table1
INNER JOIN table2 ON table1.common_column = table2.common_column;
```

If a row in either table has no match, it is excluded.

slides.title: INNER JOIN Example
Result Explanation 📋
slides.content:
From our sample data, the result would be:
```
name    | city   | order_id | amount
--------|--------|----------|-------
Alice   | London | 101      | 250
Alice   | London | 103      | 320
Bob     | Paris  | 102      | 180
```
- Charlie (customer 3) is missing because he has no orders.
- Order 104 is missing because its customer_id=4 doesn’t exist in customers.

INNER JOIN returns only the intersection.

quizData.question: If you INNER JOIN a table with 3 rows and a table with 4 rows where only 2 rows match the join condition, how many rows will the result have?

slides.title: Selecting Columns from Both Tables 🎯
slides.content:
You can pick columns from either table. If column names are unique, you can use them directly; otherwise, prefix with table name or alias.

```sql
SELECT c.name, o.amount
FROM customers c
INNER JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id;
```

Using aliases (`c`, `o`) makes queries shorter and more readable.

slides.title: Alias Example

quizData.question: If both tables have a column 'id', how do you refer to orders.id?
quizData.explanation: Prefix with table name (or alias) to resolve ambiguity.

slides.title: INNER JOIN with Conditions ⚙️
slides.content:
You can add WHERE clauses to filter further. The join condition and filter condition are separate:

```sql
SELECT c.name, o.amount
FROM customers c
INNER JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
WHERE o.amount > 200;
```
This returns only matching orders with amount > 200.

slides.content: Write an INNER JOIN query to show customer name, order ID, and amount for orders where amount is less than 300. Use the sample tables.
